category_title: Highly anxious students with bipolar disorder who thrive in low-pressure environments
student_description: Shirley is a 61-year-old student with bipolar affective disorder who carries severe trauma from past educational experiences, making her terrified of ridicule and highly sensitive to pressure. She uniquely requires an environment completely devoid of time or performance pressure, where teachers actively model vulnerability and explicitly guarantee that mistakes and mental health relapses are accommodated.

criteria.rationale: Shirley's deep-seated fear of ridicule from past school trauma is only bypassed when the authority figure explicitly normalizes mistakes and admits their own fallibility.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly states that mistakes are acceptable or minor, AND/OR models vulnerability by admitting to their own mistakes or lack of perfection.

criteria.rationale: Any hint of time limits, performance expectations, or formal assessment will cause Shirley to immediately withdraw from the environment.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly removes any time constraints, performance expectations, or assessment criteria from the immediate task.

criteria.rationale: A rigid, formal, 'school-like' approach triggers Shirley's past educational trauma.
criteria.check: The tutor uses a warm, informal conversational style (e.g., using first names, avoiding rigid authoritative commands) to distance the interaction from traditional school environments.

criteria.rationale: Discussing her mental health history can cause acute distress that requires immediate cessation of the activity to protect her well-being.
criteria.check: If the student exhibits distress (particularly regarding her mental health history), the tutor immediately suspends the task or line of questioning without pushing her to continue.
